Town and Country Planning Act 1990 section 77
National Planning Policy Framework decision making

official_measurement_examples.name: 2026 Direction current
official_measurement_examples.fact: The Town and Country Planning Consultation England Direction 2026 was published 31 March 2026 and operates alongside the 2024 Direction rather than replacing it.

official_measurement_examples.name: Grant versus refusal referral
official_measurement_examples.fact: Current determining guidance distinguishes the 2024 Direction for specified minded-to-grant cases from the 2026 Direction for specified minded-to-refuse cases.

official_measurement_examples.name: Large housing refusal referral
official_measurement_examples.fact: The Chief Planner's 17 April 2026 letter explains the 2026 Direction referral for schemes including 150 or more dwellings where an LPA intends to refuse, with a Secretary of State consideration period.

official_measurement_examples.name: Referral is not call-in
official_measurement_examples.fact: Consultation with the Secretary of State creates an opportunity to consider call-in; referral itself is not a call-in decision or a final planning decision.

official_measurement_examples.name: Call-in effect
official_measurement_examples.fact: If an application is called in under section 77, the Secretary of State rather than the local planning authority determines whether permission should be granted.

official_measurement_examples.name: Formal decision boundary
official_measurement_examples.fact: Government consultation material states individual call-in is not possible after the local planning authority has issued its formal decision notice, so referral and decision timing must be retained.

official_measurement_examples.name: Current called-in decisions
official_measurement_examples.fact: The called-in decisions and recovered appeals collection was updated 16 July 2026 and must be treated as decision evidence, not as a universal rule for other sites.

official_measurement_examples.name: Guidance versus statutory Direction
official_measurement_examples.fact: Called-in procedural guidance explains process but does not replace the statutory Direction, section 77 power or the individual Secretary of State decision.

core_rules: minded-to-grant and minded-to-refuse referral routes must not be collapsed
Secretary of State referral is not a call-in decision
LPA resolution is not final decision while statutory referral applies
formal decision timing matters to call-in availability
consultation proposals are not current Directions unless enacted
procedural guidance is not the statutory Direction
section77 call-in changes decision maker but not land ownership
call-in status does not calculate parcel development yield
historic referrals retain date and outcome
absence from a decision collection is not proof no referral occurred
no parcel call-in clearance may be inferred from generic policy
no Future Growth promotion while recovery is parked
source_verification_note: Official MHCLG, Planning Inspectorate, GOV.UK and legislation.gov.uk sources checked on 2026-07-26. March-April 2026 Consultation Direction changes and July 2026 called-in guidance/decision updates were preserved with referral, call-in and final-decision separation; no parcel promotion.
